text.en: Raju held a diamond ring and a pencil lead. "Both are carbon!" said his teacher, and he could hardly believe it.

Carbon is the main constituent of coal and forms two classes of compounds: organic and inorganic. It has special features. Catenation is the ability of carbon atoms to join in long chains and rings, and tetravalency means carbon has four bonds. Carbon can form single, double and triple bonds, which is why there are so many carbon compounds.
Isomerism is the phenomenon in which the same molecular formula has different structural arrangements, and such compounds are isomers; C2H6O is an example. Allotropy is the existence of an element in different forms: diamond, graphite and fullerene are crystalline forms of carbon while charcoal and coke are amorphous.
Plastics are catenated carbon compounds. They are useful but harm the environment because they do not decay. New rules ban some single-use plastic items, and students can help by refusing, reusing and recycling plastic in daily life.

problem.en: Name two crystalline forms of carbon.

text.en: Crystalline forms have regular arrangements of atoms.
Diamond and graphite are two examples.

prompt.en: A friend says Diamond and graphite are different elements. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: Both are made only of carbon.
They are allotropes with different atom arrangements.

points.en: Isomers share a formula but differ in structure.
Allotropes are different forms of one element.
